name: Capture orders and run pre-trade compliance checks
summary: Every public market order from the fund's systematic strategies, discretionary and fundamental portfolio managers and the balancing and currency teams enters the order management system before the central trading desk works it. The system enriches the order, tests it against the restricted list, the statutory 10% issuer and 30% voting share limits, mandate limits and short sale rules, and either passes it, warns the portfolio manager or blocks it for Compliance. A trader then accepts the order and plans large ones. Most orders pass in minutes; the slow and error-prone cases are false blocks from stale positions, overrides that need a reason and later review, hard-to-borrow shorts, re-keyed baskets and orders queried by the desk.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager with a central trading desk that executes public equity, rates, FX and listed derivative orders for all investment departments and the Balancing Portfolio.
baseline.notes: Credit orders are excluded because Credit Investments executes its own public credit trades. Execution, booking and settlement are separate processes.

trigger: A portfolio decision or a rebalancing or currency trade list reaches the order management system.
end_state: The order has passed pre-trade compliance and been accepted by a trader (with an execution plan for large orders), or it has been cancelled or withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: Higher in volatile markets (March 2020), at quarter-ends, index rebalancing dates and large balancing trades; lower in late December and summer.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (driver public_orders, about 1,200 orders a trading day); the fund does not publish order counts.

Central desk executes public orders for all departments (F2021). FTE is the author's estimate from about 1.2 minutes of trader time per order at 25,000 orders a month, within the 6.3 FTE of trader headcount not claimed by other workflows. Loaded cost from the organisation file (estimated total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead factor 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Stands in for every portfolio manager who answers compliance alerts, amends rejected orders or clarifies instructions (CMF, Active Equities and TFM). FTE from hands-on time times volume. Loaded cost from the organisation file (estimated total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead factor 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Releases model-generated order batches for the systematic strategies; FTE from about 0.2 minutes per systematic order. Loaded cost from the organisation file (estimated total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead factor 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

systems.name: Order and execution management system with pre-trade compliance rules
SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists
Global custodian web portal and statements

steps.name: Receive portfolio decision or trade list
steps.description: A portfolio decision or a rebalancing or currency trade list reaches the order system from one of four sources: a systematic strategy run, a discretionary CMF portfolio manager, the Total Fund Management balancing or currency team, or an Active Equities portfolio manager. The system records the source, the portfolio and the time received.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: balancing or currency trade list from TFM

evidence.note: Origin shares by order count are the author's estimate: systematic strategies produce many small orders, balancing and currency programs send baskets, and fundamental decisions produce few orders. The central desk serving all teams is stated in F2021.

steps.name: Generate orders from the strategy target portfolio
steps.description: At a scheduled run the strategy engine compares target positions with current holdings, converts the differences into child orders with quantity, side, account and order type, and loads the batch into the order management system as a staged list.

error.defect_description: Stale prices or positions in the strategy input produce wrong quantities.

evidence.note: Batch schedule and generation method are the author's estimate for systematic strategies; plan's tools are not public.

steps.name: Review and release the strategy order batch
steps.description: A CMF associate opens the staged batch, compares order count, gross and net notional and turnover with the expected size of the run, spot-checks the largest orders against prices on Bloomberg, and releases the batch, or rejects it and asks for a rerun when the totals look wrong.

error.defect_description: A wrong quantity in a large batch is not spotted.

control.basis: Model output check before release (four-eyes review of systematic order batches under CMF trading controls)

next.condition: batch looks right and is released
batch rejected and rerun after a data fix

evidence.note: Per-order time is a batch review spread over its orders; rerun share is the author's estimate. Separate staging and checking steps are a known source of breaks (LSEG).

steps.name: Enter a discretionary order
steps.description: A CMF macro or discretionary portfolio manager opens the order ticket, picks the instrument, side, quantity or notional and account, and types instructions for the desk such as urgency, limit price and benchmark, then submits the order to compliance checking.

error.defect_description: Wrong account, side or quantity keyed.

evidence.note: Hands-on time for a manual order ticket is the author's estimate. cmf_principal stands in for the originating portfolio manager (CMF, Active Equities or TFM).

steps.name: Stage balancing or currency orders from the trade list
steps.description: A TFM associate uploads the approved basket of futures, ETF, swap, cash equity or FX forward orders from the trade list spreadsheet into the order system, checks that the uploaded count and notional match the list, and submits the basket to compliance checking.

error.defect_description: Re-keying from the spreadsheet gives a wrong quantity or instrument.

evidence.note: Same work as step s15 of pim-tf-balancing-rebalance seen per order: a 20-minute list upload spread over about 300 orders a day. Duplicate data entry between separate tools is described by LSEG.

steps.name: Enter an Active Equities order
steps.description: An Active Equities portfolio manager enters the buy, sell, short or cover order that follows a portfolio decision and the optimiser's sizing, choosing quantity, account and instructions such as limit, participation rate and time horizon, and submits it to compliance checking.

error.defect_description: Wrong side (short instead of sell) or quantity keyed.

evidence.note: Long/short portfolio built by optimisation (F2022); entry time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enrich the order and validate static data
steps.description: The order system looks up the security master, account, settlement market, lot size and price tolerance, adds default broker lists and trade date, and rejects orders whose security or account is missing or inactive.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: security or account not set up or incomplete

evidence.note: Share of orders needing a new security is the author's estimate; security set-up as a control area is in the SIFMA guide.

steps.name: Set up or fix the security record
steps.description: An investment data analyst receives the exception, looks the instrument up in vendor reference data, creates or corrects the security master record with identifiers, market and settlement details, has it checked by a second analyst, and releases it so the order can be revalidated.

error.defect_description: Wrong settlement market or identifier set up.

control.basis: New securities and changes to securities authorised and processed accurately (SOC 1 baseline control objective)

next.condition: record set up; revalidate the order

evidence.note: Control objective from SIFMA; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run pre-trade compliance rules
steps.description: The compliance engine tests the order against the restricted list, the statutory 10% issuer and 30% voting share limits, ownership reporting thresholds, program mandate limits, short sale rules, counterparty limits for OTC trades and foreign ownership limits, and returns pass, soft warning or hard block.

error.defect_description: Stale start-of-day positions or a mis-coded rule give a false pass or false block.

control.basis: The model fund Regulations s.11 (10% of assets in one issuer) and s.13 (30% of voting shares); insider trading prohibitions in securities law; short selling rules

evidence.note: Statutory limits are tier A in the Regulations; pass, warning and block shares are the author's estimate, as no published rate was found.

steps.name: Review a soft warning and record the override reason
steps.description: The portfolio manager opens the warning, checks the projected position against the threshold (for example an approach to an ownership reporting level or a program concentration limit), and either types an override reason, reduces the order or cancels it.

error.defect_description: Override reason too thin to support later review.

control.basis: Investment compliance policy: documented reason for every soft-warning override

evidence.note: Workflow after a tripped rule is the main pre-trade challenge (Markets Media); shares are the author's estimate. cmf_principal stands in for the originating portfolio manager (CMF, Active Equities or TFM).

steps.name: Investigate a hard block
steps.description: A compliance officer opens the blocked order, checks why the rule fired (restricted list entry, statutory limit calculation, foreign ownership room or counterparty limit), confirms positions with the data owner or the deal team, and clears false blocks, refers an exception or rejects the order back to the portfolio manager.

error.defect_description: A real breach is cleared as a data issue.

control.basis: Insider trading prohibitions (for example Ontario Securities Act s.76) and the model fund Regulations investment limits; Compliance clears blocked orders

next.condition: false block from stale or wrong data, cleared
rejected back to the portfolio manager

evidence.note: Compliance supervisors approve or reject blocked trades (Bloomberg); outcome shares and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide on a compliance exception
steps.description: The compliance director reads the officer's note and the portfolio manager's request, for example a temporary limit excess caused by an index event, decides whether an exception is allowed under policy and records the decision and any conditions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Exceptions to investment restrictions approved by Compliance management, not by the portfolio manager

evidence.note: Exception path and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Amend or cancel a rejected order
steps.description: The portfolio manager reads the rejection reason, then resizes the order, picks another instrument (for example a swap instead of a physical short) or cancels the order, and resubmits any amended order to compliance checking.

error.defect_description: Amended order keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate. cmf_principal stands in for the originating portfolio manager (CMF, Active Equities or TFM).

steps.name: Check borrow availability for short sales
steps.description: For sell orders that would create or add to a short position, the order system checks the prime brokers' easy-to-borrow list and attaches the locate; long sales and buys pass straight through. Hard-to-borrow names are held for a manual locate.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Regulation SHO Rule 203(b)(1) locate before a short sale; EU Short Selling Regulation requires short sales of shares to be covered

next.condition: not a short sale or on the easy-to-borrow list

evidence.note: Locate and covered short rules are stated by the SEC and ESMA; share of hard-to-borrow orders is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request a locate from the prime broker
steps.description: A trader sends the security and quantity to one or more prime brokers through their locate tool or chat, asks for the borrow rate, and records the locate reference on the order.

error.defect_description: Locate reference not recorded on the order.

control.basis: Regulation SHO Rule 203(b)(1): locate made and documented before effecting the short sale

evidence.note: Locate documentation requirement from the SEC; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the prime broker's locate answer
steps.description: The prime broker's stock loan desk checks its inventory and replies with an approved quantity and rate, a partial amount or a refusal. Scarce names can take longer or need several brokers.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: no borrow; portfolio manager must amend or cancel

evidence.note: Response times and refusal share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the order to the trading blotter
steps.description: The order system routes the cleared order to the blotter of the right desk by asset class and region and timestamps the release, so it is visible to the traders on duty.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Central desk by asset class and region (F2021); routing is generic.

steps.name: Review and accept the order
steps.description: A trader checks the order against the market: size against average daily volume, instructions, limit price against the current price, upcoming events and whether the market is open. Most orders are accepted in one click, some baskets in bulk; unclear or unusual orders are queried.

error.defect_description: Accepted order with an unnoticed error.

control.basis: Central trading model: orders executed by the central desk, separate from the portfolio manager who decides them

next.condition: large against daily volume or above desk size guidance
instructions unclear or order looks wrong
pre-funded market needs a cash check
obvious error, rejected to the portfolio manager

evidence.note: Central desk independent of investment teams (F2021); shares and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Query the order with the portfolio manager
steps.description: The trader messages or calls the portfolio manager to confirm quantity, side, limit or urgency, or to point out a likely keying error, and notes the query on the order.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Clarify or amend the order
steps.description: The portfolio manager answers the query: confirms the order as entered, amends it (which sends it back through compliance checks) or withdraws it.

error.defect_description: Amendment introduces a new error.

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate. cmf_principal stands in for the originating portfolio manager (CMF, Active Equities or TFM).

steps.name: Plan the execution of a large order
steps.description: For an order that is large against daily volume or above desk size guidance, the trader estimates market impact and cost with the pre-trade tool, picks a benchmark and horizon, splits the work across regional desks if needed and records the plan on the order.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Large balancing trades need impact management (F2021 desk description); time and share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the override in the daily exception report
steps.description: The next morning a compliance officer reviews the list of overridden warnings, checks each reason against the rule and the resulting position, and follows up with the portfolio manager where the reason is weak. This review does not hold up the order.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Investment guideline compliance and guideline breach review (SOC 1 control area); audit trail of overrides

next.condition: order continues while the review runs

evidence.note: Guideline compliance as a control area (SIFMA); review time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm cash pre-funding at the custodian
steps.description: For a buy in a market that requires cash before trading, a settlements analyst checks the local currency balance on the custodian portal, arranges an FX conversion or transfer if short, and confirms to the desk that the order can be worked.

error.defect_description: Cash not in place in time; trade fails or is delayed.

control.basis: Local market pre-funding rules in some emerging markets

evidence.note: Pre-funding practice is the author's knowledge of emerging market custody; share and times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Security not set up
exceptions.description: The instrument or account is missing from the security master, so the order waits for an investment data analyst to create the record.

exceptions.name: Soft warning overridden
exceptions.description: The order approaches a threshold; the portfolio manager records a reason and Compliance reviews it the next morning.

exceptions.name: Hard block rejected
exceptions.description: The order hits the restricted list or a statutory or mandate limit; Compliance rejects it and the portfolio manager amends or cancels.

exceptions.name: False block from stale positions
exceptions.description: Start-of-day positions are late or wrong, so a limit appears breached; Compliance confirms positions and clears the block.

exceptions.name: Hard-to-borrow short
exceptions.description: A short sale is not on the easy-to-borrow list; the trader gets a manual locate, and without borrow the order is amended or cancelled.

exceptions.name: Order queried by the desk
exceptions.description: The trader questions quantity, side or instructions; amendments go back through compliance checks.

exceptions.name: Pre-funded market
exceptions.description: A buy in a market that requires cash before trading waits for settlements to confirm local currency at the custodian.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the decision or trade list reaching the order system to trader acceptance
benchmarks.population: Orders at a large multi-strategy institutional investor with a central desk

evidence.note: No published statistic. Author's estimate: most orders pass checks in seconds and are accepted within one to two hours of staging, since systematic batches are staged before the open; queried, blocked and locate cases take hours.

benchmarks.unit: share of votes to elect directors of one corporation

evidence.note: The model fund Regulations section 13(1).

benchmarks.unit: share of total book value of assets in securities of one person

evidence.note: The model fund Regulations section 11(1).

benchmarks.unit: share of issued share capital (public disclosure from 0.005)
benchmarks.population: Net short positions in EU shares

evidence.note: Threshold as stated on the ESMA page; the threshold in force earlier in the reference period may have been higher.
C$63 million in transaction costs.

pain_points.description: Balancing and currency baskets are built in spreadsheets and uploaded to the order system, so quantities are re-keyed and checked twice.

evidence.note: Duplicate data entry between separate decision, order and execution tools (LSEG).

pain_points.description: Most compliance alerts are false positives caused by stale start-of-day positions, index events or coarse rules, and each one interrupts a portfolio manager or a compliance officer.

evidence.note: Workflow after tripped rules is the main challenge (Markets Media); false-positive share is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Long/short and derivative strategies need rules for net exposure, short sales and counterparty limits that generic pre-trade engines handle poorly.

evidence.note: Leveraged and long/short managers find pre-trade compliance harder (Markets Media); Active Equities is long/short (F2022).

pain_points.description: Order, compliance and execution tools were separate during the period; the fund was building an integrated public markets trading platform, so status chasing between tools was common.

evidence.note: Multi-year integrated platform initiative (F2021).

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: Active Equities builds a concentrated long/short market-neutral portfolio through an optimisation that removes unintended factor exposures; gross assets C$74 billion; trading fees rising with the size and complexity of public market activity

sources.title: The model fund Regulations (SOR/99-190)
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: Section 11: no more than 10% of the book value of assets in securities of one person or associated persons (index-replicating funds exempt); section 13: no investment in a corporation whose securities carry more than 30% of the votes to elect directors; section 16: related-party transaction prohibition

sources.title: Key Points About Regulation SHO
sources.supports: Rule 203(b)(1): a broker-dealer must have reasonable grounds to believe the security can be borrowed, and the locate must be made and documented before effecting a short sale

sources.title: Short Selling (Markets and Infrastructure)
sources.supports: EU short selling rules: all short sales of shares must be covered; net short positions reported to regulators from 0.1% of issued share capital and disclosed publicly from 0.5%

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.supports: Baseline control objectives: trades authorised and processed in accordance with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; new securities and changes to securities authorised and processed accurately; investment guideline and restriction compliance, trade errors and guideline breaches, insider trading and cross trading as control areas

sources.title: Trading & Investment Compliance Solutions
sources.supports: Compliance enforced at trade entry and execution inside the order management system; automated alerts let compliance supervisors review and approve or reject blocked trades; potential rule breaches flagged so users can adjust intent before orders move forward

sources.title: Reducing PMS, OMS and EMS workflow breaks
sources.publisher: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG Data & Analytics)
sources.supports: Workflow breaks arise when investment decisions, order creation, compliance checks, staging and execution sit in separate workflows, causing duplicate data entry, status chasing, repeated checks and manual reconciliation

sources.title: Buy Side Assesses Pre-Trade Compliance
sources.supports: Long-only equity managers with current pre-trade compliance engines cope with new rules, while leveraged, long/short and derivative users find it harder; the main challenges are workflow once a pre-trade rule has tripped

assumptions: The process starts when an order request reaches the order system and ends at trader acceptance; working the order, broker routing and fills belong to pim-mkt-execute-trades, which starts from the accepted order on the blotter.
Origin shares by order count (systematic 55%, balancing 27%, currency 10%, Active Equities 8%) are the author's estimates; the fund publishes no order counts.

Balancing orders are uploaded as baskets. The list-level staging, compliance alert handling and trader acceptance already appear in pim-tf-balancing-rebalance (steps s15 to s18); here the same work is seen per order, so tfm_associate time per order is tiny and its fte_on_process is kept at 0.1 to avoid double counting.

cmf_principal stands in for the originating portfolio manager when answering warnings, amending rejected orders and clarifying queries, because the step graph cannot remember which team sent the order.
Pass, soft warning and hard block shares (94.5%, 4%, 1.5%) and their outcomes are estimates; no published rate of pre-trade alerts was found.

The organisation file lists no process that sends the restricted list to order capture; restricted_list_update is taken as a standing input from lc-negotiate-close, which is the only producer in the file.

compliance_director, data_ops_analyst, cmf_associate and set_analyst are organisation roles not listed for this process; they are added for exception approval, security set-up, batch release and pre-funding checks.
cmf_trading_director is listed for the process but takes no step here; desk-head sign-off on large or sensitive orders is modelled in pim-mkt-execute-trades (step s07).
Credit orders are out of scope because Credit Investments executes its own public credit trades.
The next-morning review of overrides does not delay the order and is modelled as a concurrent step with no wait.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file and include large incentive pay, so labour cost per order is high relative to the minutes spent.
